codex.nav.tagline.note: Subtitle beside the URIM brand in the reader's masthead. The reader is styled as an illuminated medieval manuscript; keep a bookish, slightly solemn register and the lowercase.

codex.nav.read.note: Tab: the chapter text, laid out as a manuscript page

codex.nav.people.note: Tab: the index of everyone and everything the story names

codex.nav.map.note: Tab: the map of the story's lands and journeys

codex.nav.hours.note: Tab: the story day by day with the ancient hours. Named after the medieval prayer book (Latin 'liber horarum'); use your language's name for that kind of manuscript if it has one (Russian: Часослов).

codex.nav.not_translated.note: After a chapter in the selector: '1 Kings 17 · not yet translated' (no new translation of any verse yet)

codex.nav.translated_of.note: After a chapter in the selector: '1 Kings 17 · 12 of 24 translated'; counts verses

codex.nav.search.note: Placeholder of the search box; 'the codex' is this illuminated reader

codex.nav.by_meaning.note: Beside a search result found by similarity of meaning rather than by matching words

codex.nav.war_room.note: Link to the review app, called the War Room; ↗ means it opens the other app

codex.nav.war_room_title.note: Tooltip of the War Room link

codex.fallback.title.text: Not yet translated into this language: shown in English
codex.fallback.title.note: Tooltip of the small 'EN' marker beside a text that has no translation in the chosen language and falls back to English (the only fallback language)

codex.folio.empty.text: The codex is empty: nothing has been ingested yet.
codex.folio.empty.note: The reader has no chapters at all; 'ingested' means loaded from the sources

codex.folio.opening.note: Loading a chapter; a folio is a manuscript page. Keep the manuscript image.

codex.folio.chapter.note: Heading of the page; {roman} is a Roman numeral such as XVII

codex.folio.prev_chapter.note: Link to the previous chapter at the foot of the page; {roman} is a Roman numeral. Flip the arrow for right-to-left languages.

codex.folio.next_chapter.note: Link to the next chapter at the foot of the page; {roman} is a Roman numeral. Flip the arrow for right-to-left languages.

codex.folio.baseline.kjv.note: Button naming the traditional translation shown by default: the King James Version. Use the name readers of your language know it by.

codex.folio.baseline.synodal.note: Button naming the traditional translation shown by default: the Russian Synodal Bible

codex.folio.baseline_mark.kjv.note: Short name of the King James Version, shown in parentheses beside a verse that has no new translation yet

codex.folio.baseline_mark.synodal.note: Short name of the Russian Synodal Bible, shown in parentheses beside a verse that has no new translation yet

codex.folio.layer.literal.note: Button and label: the ultra-literal translation, which follows the Hebrew word order

codex.folio.layer.dramatic.note: Button and label: the dramatic translation, written to be read aloud like a play

codex.folio.layer_none.literal.text: No word-for-word translation of this chapter yet: the {baseline} text is shown.
codex.folio.layer_none.literal.note: {baseline} is the traditional translation's name, e.g. 'King James'

codex.folio.layer_none.dramatic.text: No dramatic translation of this chapter yet: the {baseline} text is shown.
codex.folio.layer_none.dramatic.note: {baseline} is the traditional translation's name, e.g. 'King James'

codex.folio.layer_partial.literal.one: The word-for-word translation covers {covered} of {count} verse so far; the rest show the {baseline} text, marked ({mark}).
codex.folio.layer_partial.literal.other: The word-for-word translation covers {covered} of {count} verses so far; the rest show the {baseline} text, marked ({mark}).
codex.folio.layer_partial.literal.note: {count} is the chapter's verses, {covered} those translated; {baseline} names the traditional translation ('King James'), {mark} its short form shown beside each such verse ('KJV')

codex.folio.layer_partial.dramatic.one: The dramatic translation covers {covered} of {count} verse so far; the rest show the {baseline} text, marked ({mark}).
codex.folio.layer_partial.dramatic.other: The dramatic translation covers {covered} of {count} verses so far; the rest show the {baseline} text, marked ({mark}).
codex.folio.layer_partial.dramatic.note: {count} is the chapter's verses, {covered} those translated; {baseline} names the traditional translation ('King James'), {mark} its short form shown beside each such verse ('KJV')

codex.folio.marks_title.note: Tooltip of the fleuron ❦ beside a verse that has commentary or notes on words

codex.folio.verse_count.note: At the foot of the page: '24 verses · 9 events · tap a verse to unfold it'

codex.folio.event_count.note: At the foot of the page: '24 verses · 9 events · tap a verse to unfold it'

codex.folio.tap_to_unfold.text: tap a verse to unfold it
codex.folio.tap_to_unfold.note: At the foot of the page; a verse opens to show its words, translations and notes

codex.folio.showing.note: Under the page when one verse is open; {ref} is a chapter:verse reference like 17:4

codex.folio.test_yourself.note: Link to the quizzes on this chapter in the War Room

codex.folio.hebrew_words.note: Small-caps heading inside an opened verse: each Hebrew word with its transliteration and gloss

codex.folio.aliases.note: Where the Hebrew verse numbering differs from the King James one; {refs} like 'KJV 18:34'. Name the Bibles of your language's tradition if the numbering there follows the KJV.

codex.folio.translations.note: Small-caps heading inside an opened verse

codex.folio.no_translations.text: No new translations for this verse yet; the word glosses come from STEPBible.
codex.folio.no_translations.note: STEPBible is the name of the source of the word glosses; keep it

codex.folio.commentary.note: Small-caps heading inside an opened verse: historical and linguistic commentary

codex.folio.notes.note: Small-caps heading inside an opened verse: notes on key Hebrew words

codex.folio.root.note: In a note on a word: its Hebrew root, e.g. 'root שׁוב'

codex.folio.in_this_verse.note: Small-caps heading inside an opened verse, above the people, places and events it names

codex.folio.word.gloss.note: The English meaning of a Hebrew word in quotation marks; use your language's quotation marks

codex.folio.word.from.note: Label on a Hebrew word's card: the dictionary form it comes from

codex.folio.word.form.note: Label on a Hebrew word's card: its grammar (verb qal perfect…)

codex.folio.word.strongs.note: Label on a Hebrew word's card: its Strong's concordance number

codex.folio.word.reading.note: Label on a Hebrew word's card: a note on how the word is read aloud

codex.folio.word.qere.note: Qere and Ketiv are the Masoretic terms for what is read and what is written; keep the two terms

codex.folio.word.names.note: Label on a Hebrew word's card: the person or place the word names

codex.hours.loading.note: Loading the Book of Hours; keep the image of turning a manuscript's pages

codex.hours.latin.note: Latin running title above 'The Book of Hours', in the manuscript voice. Keep it in Latin unless your readers' tradition has its own liturgical term (e.g. Church Slavonic).

codex.hours.title.note: Page heading: the story day by day with the ancient hours. Use your language's name for the medieval prayer book (Russian: Часослов).

codex.hours.subtitle: The story day by day, as the clock of the ancient hours tells it

codex.hours.day_month.note: A day of the month and the month's name, '14 September'; reorder for your language. {month} comes from the browser in your language.

codex.hours.same_day.note: Between two days of the story: no time passes between them

codex.hours.next_day.note: Between two days of the story

codex.hours.days_pass.note: Between two days of the story: the time that passes

codex.hours.months_pass.note: Between two days of the story: the time that passes

codex.hours.years_pass.note: Between two days of the story; {count} may be a decimal such as 2.5

codex.hours.because.fulfills.note: Under an event, linking to a later event: a prophecy here is fulfilled there. {event} is that event's title.

codex.hours.because.avenges.note: Under an event, linking to a later event that avenges it. {event} is that event's title.

codex.hours.because.enables.note: Under an event, linking to a later event it makes possible. {event} is that event's title.

codex.hours.because.other.note: Under an event, linking to a later event it causes. {event} is that event's title.

codex.hours.at_once.note: In parentheses after a consequence: it follows immediately

codex.hours.later.note: In parentheses after a consequence; {duration} like '3 d'

codex.hours.horologium.note: Latin heading of the clock dial of the ancient hours, in the manuscript voice; keep it Latin unless your tradition has its own word

codex.hours.chosen_hour.note: Small-caps heading over the event picked on the dial

codex.hours.how_we_know.note: Before the reasoning that dates the chosen event

codex.hours.the_hours.note: Heading of the list of the ancient hours of the day

codex.hours.hour.morning_watch.note: The last night watch before dawn (Hebrew ashmoret ha-boqer)

codex.hours.hour.third.note: The third hour after sunrise, about 9 o'clock (Latin hora tertia)

codex.hours.hour.minchah.note: Transliterated Hebrew: the afternoon offering and its hour; transliterate it for your script

codex.hours.hour.between_evenings.note: Literal rendering of the Hebrew bein ha-arbayim, the dusk; keep it literal

codex.hours.hour.middle_watch.note: The middle of the three night watches (Hebrew ashmoret ha-tikhonah)

codex.mappa.loading.note: Loading the map; 'chart' as an old sea or land map, unrolled like a scroll

codex.mappa.cartouche.note: Latin title in the map's cartouche ('map of the land'), with V for U as old maps write it; keep it Latin unless your tradition has its own

codex.mappa.cartouche_sub.note: Italic line under the map's Latin title

codex.mappa.credits.text: Natural Earth (public domain) · places after OpenBible.info · “?” marks an uncertain site
codex.mappa.credits.note: Credits under the map; Natural Earth and OpenBible.info are names. A '?' after a place name marks an uncertain identification.

codex.mappa.journeys.note: Heading of the list of people whose travels the map can draw

codex.mappa.stage_count.note: After a person's name in the list of journeys: the stops on their road

codex.mappa.prev_stage.note: Button: show the journey up to the previous stage

codex.mappa.next_stage.note: Button: show the journey up to the next stage

codex.mappa.whole_road.note: Button: show the whole journey at once

codex.mappa.nothing_here: Named, but nothing happens here in these chapters.

codex.mappa.read_about.note: Link from a place on the map to its page; {name} is the place's name

codex.people.loading.note: Loading the index of persons; 'the company' as a cast of characters

codex.people.latin.note: Latin running title of the index of persons, in the manuscript voice; keep it Latin unless your tradition has its own

codex.people.title.note: Page heading of the index of everyone and everything the story names

codex.people.subtitle: Everyone and everything the story names, in order of importance

codex.people.group.persons.note: Section heading in the index of persons

codex.people.group.divine.note: Section heading: God and heavenly beings (angels, spirits)

codex.people.group.places.note: Section heading in the index of persons

codex.people.group.peoples.note: Section heading: nations, tribes and groups of people (prophets of Baal, the army)

codex.people.group.things.note: Section heading: objects and substances (the altar, the flour)

codex.people.type.PERSON.note: Small-caps kind above a name on its page

codex.people.type.DEITY.note: Small-caps kind above God's name, or a god's, on its page

codex.people.type.SPIRIT_BEING.note: Small-caps kind above an angel's or spirit's name on its page

codex.people.type.LOCATION.note: Small-caps kind above a place's name on its page

codex.people.type.GROUP.note: Small-caps kind above a group's name on its page: a people or nation, not 'persons'

codex.people.type.ARTIFACT.note: Small-caps kind above a made thing's name on its page

codex.people.type.SUBSTANCE.note: Small-caps kind above a substance's name on its page (oil, flour, water)

codex.people.like.note: Section heading over others of the same kind whose description is nearest in meaning; {name} is the person or place on the page

codex.people.opening.note: Loading a person's or place's page

codex.people.also_called.note: Other names of the person or place, separated by commas

codex.people.name_means.note: Small-caps lead-in before the meaning of the Hebrew name

codex.people.located.note: Coordinates of a place; N and E are north latitude and east longitude

codex.people.approximate.note: After the coordinates when the site's identification is uncertain

codex.people.in_story.note: Section heading over the events a person or place takes part in

codex.people.at_place.note: Where an event happens; {place} is a place's name

codex.people.through_narrative.note: Section heading over the states a person holds over the story (widowed, hiding, fed by ravens)

codex.people.state_until.note: How long a state lasts; {state} is the kind of state in lowercase (may be empty), {from} and {until} are chapter:verse references like 17:4

codex.people.state_onward.note: A state that lasts to the end of the story; {state} is the kind of state in lowercase (may be empty), {from} a chapter:verse reference

codex.people.deeds.note: Section heading over what a person does to or with others

codex.people.named_in.note: Section heading over the verses that mention the person or place

codex.people.all.note: Link back to the index of persons and places
